title: Salesforce (CRM) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Lift As AI And Braze Views Evolve
detail:
Salesforce (CRM) Stock Sees Modest Fair Value Lift As AI And Braze Views Evolve
Bailey Pemberton

CRM
BRZE
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Salesforce's fair value estimate has shifted from US$281.08 to US$287.08, a modest adjustment that reflects updated assumptions in the current analyst models. Recent research links this change to a mixed but generally constructive view around the Braze acquisition, clearer AI monetization paths, and Salesforce's role in customer engagement software, with some firms using these factors to support price targets in the US$250 to US$300 range. As you read on, you will see how this evolving narrative might shape the way you track Salesforce from here.

Analyst Price Targets don't always capture the full story. Head over to our Company Report to find new ways to value Salesforce.

What Wall Street Has Been Saying
🐂 Bullish Takeaways

Several firms, including Guggenheim, Stifel, Canaccord, TD Cowen, Cantor Fitzgerald, BMO Capital, Mizuho and Argus, have raised Salesforce price targets into the US$280 to US$300 area, citing clearer AI monetization paths, product momentum and confidence in long term company targets discussed at Dreamforce and recent investor events.

Jefferies and DA Davidson point to the Braze acquisition as a positive for Salesforce, with Jefferies expecting it to re energize Marketing and Commerce Cloud and DA Davidson highlighting the opportunity to strengthen a weaker part of the platform while using capital at what it views as reasonable Braze valuation levels.

RBC Capital and JPMorgan describe recent Salesforce events as incrementally positive. They reference AI Force and Agentforce as important product directions and see the company articulating more concrete drivers for monetization across its installed base.

🐻 Bearish Takeaways

Evercore ISI acknowledges the logic of the Braze deal but flags that the timing and price are likely to be debated. The firm also notes that the pace of mergers and acquisitions at Salesforce could concern value and GARP oriented investors.

Wells Fargo and Citi, which both keep more neutral stances with price targets clustered around US$205 to US$263, cite mixed signals on customer spending, pricing and AI monetization, which can leave some investors cautious about paying higher valuations for Salesforce shares.

Do your thoughts align with the Bull or Bear Analysts? Perhaps you think there's more to the story. Head to the Simply Wall St Community to discover more perspectives!

How This Changes the Fair Value For Salesforce

The Fair Value estimate has moved from US$281.08 to US$287.08.

The revenue growth assumption has shifted from 10.14% to 10.02%.

The profit margin expectation is 18.22%, described as broadly stable.

The future P/E assumption has moved from 22.66x to 23.13x.

The discount rate has shifted from 9.21% to 9.08%.

Bandwidth Sinks 13% on In-Line Guidance Despite Q3 Beat: "More Conversations Between People and Agents" ©onkey Business Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Bandwidth shares fell 13% as in-line full-year guidance overshadowed a third-quarter beat.

The guidance implies slower fourth-quarter growth after a sharp run-up in the stock's valuation.

CEO David Morken says AI agents will drive more voice and text traffic, and a new Salesforce deal backs him up.

Rival Twilio makes the same AI-agent pitch, so its next outlook faces the same test.

Bandwidth (BAND:NASDAQ) posted a record quarter this morning and still sank 13%, as its full-year guidance only matched expectations.

Its growth case rests on AI agents, the same pitch rival Twilio (TWLO:NYSE) makes. And this quarter, Salesforce (CRM:NYSE) named Bandwidth its first certified international carrier for its native Contact Center.

TIKR tracks 7 analysts on Bandwidth. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Bandwidth, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Bandwidth's Analyst Ratings

The beat wasn't enough

Third-quarter revenue rose 22% to a record $234 million, just above the $233.15 million analysts expected.

But 2026 guidance of $905 million to $910 million in revenue and $1.73 to $1.79 in adjusted EPS lands right on consensus of $905.7 million and $1.75. Analysts already expected that much for 2026, and a far smaller gain for 2027:

Bandwidth (BAND): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2023-2027 (TIKR)

Nothing in that range moves the 2026 estimates. It also implies fourth-quarter growth of roughly 17% to 19%, down from the third quarter's 22%.

That's a tough sell for a stock that traded at 26x forward earnings before the report, up from 6.9x in February:

Bandwidth (BAND): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)
Agents need phone lines

CEO David Morken said AI agents "will need to reach people by voice and text." He added that Bandwidth "will continue to scale as SI generates more conversations between people and agents." (SI is Bandwidth's term for super intelligence.)

The deal takes Bandwidth's network into Salesforce's contact center in more than 25 countries. For Salesforce, it's one piece of a bigger push: Agentforce annual recurring revenue passed $1.5 billion as of July 31. Salesforce's early-December report should show how much of that agent work runs over the phone.

In August, Twilio raised its 2026 organic growth outlook to 13% to 13.5%, from 9.5% to 10.5%, and it trades at 41x forward earnings. If in-line guidance did this to Bandwidth, Twilio's outlook faces a higher bar in its third-quarter report.

The 2027 number is the one to watch

My take: Nothing here says Bandwidth's business is breaking. Free cash flow jumped to $33 million from $13 million a year earlier. The stock had just priced in more than an in-line year.

title: Salesforce vs. Synopsys: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Salesforce vs. Synopsys: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Sara Appino, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 1:36 PM EDT 6 min read
CRM
SNPS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

As artificial intelligence reshapes the enterprise landscape, choosing between a software giant and a silicon design leader is a pivotal decision. Is Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) or Synopsys (NASDAQ:SNPS) the better buy for your portfolio?

Salesforce specializes in cloud-based software that manages customer relationships, while Synopsys provides the essential tools used to design the complex chips powering modern hardware. Both businesses are prominent names in the tech sector, offering unique ways to play the ongoing digital transformation of global enterprises.

The case for Salesforce

Salesforce provides cloud-based software solutions that help organizations manage their relationships with customers across various departments. The company integrates its tools into a single platform that handles sales, service, marketing, and commerce among tech stocks. It serves a wide range of industries, including financial services and healthcare, reaching its global customer base through direct sales and a large partner ecosystem.

In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $41.5 billion, representing a growth of approximately 9.6% compared with the prior fiscal year. The company generated net income of roughly $7.5 billion during this period, resulting in a net margin of about 18%. This profitability represents an improvement over the previous fiscal year, when net income was close to $6.2 billion with a net margin of approximately 16.4%.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.3x, which is total debt divided by shareholder equity, and the current ratio was approximately 0.8x. Free cash flow reached nearly $14.4 billion, which is calculated as cash from operations minus capital expenditures. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Synopsys

Synopsys offers engineering solutions that span the entire process of creating silicon chips and electronic systems. Its software tools and intellectual property are essential for semiconductor manufacturers and systems companies working on advanced technologies like autonomous machines and data centers. The business distributes its products through a direct sales force to reach clients in the aerospace, automotive, and energy sectors.

In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Oct. 31, 2025, revenue reached approximately $7.1 billion, which was an increase of nearly 15.1% compared with the prior fiscal year. The company generated net income of roughly $1.3 billion, yielding a net margin of about 18.9%.

title: Salesforce vs. Datadog: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?

Salesforce vs. Datadog: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Mike Schwenk, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:20 PM EDT 7 min read
CRM
DDOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors often weigh established profitability against rapid expansion when choosing software stocks. Deciding whether Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) or Datadog (NASDAQ:DDOG) is the better buy depends on your preference for stability versus growth.

Salesforce provides a unified platform for customer data and AI, while Datadog offers observability and security for cloud applications. Both sell subscription software to enterprises running complex digital operations, which makes them a natural pairing for investors weighing the sector in 2026.

The case for Salesforce

Salesforce provides a comprehensive cloud platform that helps businesses manage everything from sales to agent-based AI automation. It has established itself as a leader among tech stocks in enterprise software. Its customers include organizations that utilize its Agentforce and Slack integrations.

The annual report provides no total customer count, and no single customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue, suggesting a well-diversified user base.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $41.5 billion, up about 9.6% year over year. The company reported a net income of close to $7.5 billion during this period. This performance was an improvement over the prior fiscal year, when the company recorded a net income of roughly $6.2 billion on lower total sales.

The momentum carried into the quarter ended July 31, 2026, when revenue grew 11% to $11.3 billion, and management raised its full-year outlook.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.2x. This ratio measures total borrowings relative to shareholder equity, excluding lease obligations, and it indicated a conservative use of leverage at the time. That picture has since changed.

In March 2026, Salesforce issued $25 billion in senior notes and used the proceeds to accelerate a share repurchase, so by July 31, 2026, total debt of about $39.3 billion roughly matched shareholder equity.

The current ratio, which compares current assets to current liabilities, was roughly 0.8x at fiscal year-end. Free cash flow reached nearly $14.4 billion, though note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Datadog

Datadog offers a cloud-based observability and security platform that helps organizations monitor and secure their software systems.

The company uses a land-and-expand model that has attracted about 32,700 customers in more than 160 countries. Its platform serves businesses in hybrid or public cloud environments, allowing them to act on live data to prevent outages.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 43% year over year to a record $35 million, producing a 22% adjusted EBITDA margin. Non-GAAP net income was $20 million, or $0.50 per diluted share, while free cash flow totaled $33 million.

Cloud communications and software growth

ServiceNow Sinks 19% on EPS Miss and Slower Backlog Outlook Despite "Unicorn Growth Company" Pitch ©SteveLuker from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

ServiceNow fell 19% after adjusted EPS of $1.00 missed the $1.02 consensus and it guided fourth-quarter backlog growth to 18.5%, from 20.5%.

Its rally since June came from a higher multiple, so a small miss undid much of it.

Salesforce fell with it, and the same AI worry hangs over Adobe and Intuit.

The fourth-quarter report in late January, with AI contract value and a first 2027 guide, is the next test.

ServiceNow (NOW:NYSE) sank 19% today after its third-quarter report.

Salesforce (CRM:NYSE) fell 6%. Adobe (ADBE:NASDAQ) and Intuit (INTU:NASDAQ) face the same worry: that AI agents shrink what companies pay for software.

That's a long way from what ServiceNow CEO Bill McDermott told Wednesday night's Mad Money: "this is a unicorn growth company."

A penny short, and a slower backlog

Here's the quarter:

Revenue: $4.11 billion, up 20.5%, above the $4.09 billion consensus

Adjusted EPS: $1.00, a cent under consensus

cRPO: up 20.5%, with 18.5% guided for the fourth quarter

2026 AI contract value target: raised to $1.7 billion

The backlog guide stung. But 18.5% is close to what analysts already expected. They see revenue growth slowing to about 19% in 2027:

ServiceNow (NOW): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

So I wouldn't expect big cuts to those estimates.

The price had run ahead of earnings

ServiceNow stock climbed 42% from June 30 to Oct. 12 while forward earnings rose just 4%. Its forward P/E went from 23x on June 30 to 32x at Wednesday's close:

ServiceNow (NOW): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

Today's drop takes it to about 26x, about half its five-year average of 53x.

Software sold off as a group

Salesforce's own backlog is moving the other way: its cRPO growth sped up to 14% in the quarter ended July 31. Salesforce's drop looks like investors selling the whole group.

Adobe and Intuit are already priced for the worry. Adobe traded at 9.3x forward earnings at Wednesday's close, even after raising its full-year targets in September. Intuit was at 14x after guiding fiscal 2027 revenue growth to 9-10%, down from 14%. Intuit's report in late November and Adobe's in December will show whether AI is costing them business.

My take: the quarter didn't break ServiceNow's story, and the drop took out the froth the rally had added. At about 26x forward earnings for revenue growth near 19%, the stock looks a lot more reasonable than it did on Wednesday.

Can You Still Buy Salesforce Stock Today?

Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Salesforce (CRM) shares have climbed 34.2% over the past three months, compared with 4.4% for the S&P 500. The biggest step came the day after the company released earnings in late August, when the stock jumped 23%. On the day of that release, Salesforce and Anthropic also announced an expanded partnership called Claudeforce. A buyer today pays $242.11, and that price appears to assume the quarter reported in August was not an exception. Management said that revenue for the period exceeded the top of its own forecast in constant currency. So how expensive has that run made Salesforce stock?

How Expensive Is Salesforce Against Its Own Past?

Not very. At the end of September, Salesforce traded at 4.3 times its revenue over the twelve months to July 2026. The stock ended a quarter at a lower multiple just twice out of the 40 quarter ends since fiscal 2017. Based on the October 28 close of $242.11, the shares traded at 4.5 times that same revenue.

A low price against sales is a bargain only when the company still generates as much profit on each dollar of sales as it used to. Salesforce's margins are now close to their highest since fiscal 2017. Its operating margin over the twelve months to July 2026 was 22%, coming in higher than at 37 of those 40 quarter ends.

Growth is the variable that has changed. Revenue growth over the twelve months to July 2026 was 11.2%, less than half the 24.6% recorded over the twelve months to July 2022. That leaves the stock looking fair rather than cheap: a more profitable business expanding at a slower pace.

What Salesforce Has To Deliver In Fiscal Q3

Management set revenue guidance for fiscal Q3 2027 at $11.42 billion to $11.5 billion. Analysts expect about $11.6 billion, sitting above the top of that range. The company's forecast does not include Contentful and Fin, a pair of acquisitions management expected to close in the weeks following the August 26 call. Fin staff have since joined Salesforce, and on October 20 it agreed to buy Braze for about $5.66 billion.

That guidance sets a higher bar than Salesforce's own pace in fiscal Q2 2027, when revenue grew 10.8% from a year earlier. That performance marked a slowdown from the 13.3% of fiscal Q1. Management guided growth of 11% to 12% for fiscal Q3, pointing to a pickup. That range is in constant currency, however, while the 10.8% figure is as reported.

Salesforce's contracted business is expanding faster than that guidance. Revenue under contract for the next twelve months reached $33.5 billion in fiscal Q2, up 14% in constant currency, and management expects about 14% again for fiscal Q3. Annual recurring revenue from Agentforce reached $1.5 billion, management said on the same call.
